subsystems.name: Vacuum chamber and accelerator ring
subsystems.role: provides a near-vacuum circular path where the projectile is spun up without air drag.
parts: large circular steel or composite chamber

subsystems.name: Rotor and tether
subsystems.role: carries the projectile and accelerates it along the ring to hypersonic speed.

subsystems.name: Drive and bearings
subsystems.role: spins the rotor to high speed with minimal friction.

subsystems.name: Projectile and payload
subsystems.role: the ruggedised package that survives spin-up and atmospheric release.

subsystems.name: Release and launch exit
subsystems.role: opens the vacuum chamber at the right instant and lets the projectile fly out.

subsystems.name: Ground support and control
subsystems.role: supplies power, vacuum, and precise timing for launch.

buildSteps.title: Choose site and build the chamber
buildSteps.detail: A large circular vacuum chamber is constructed at a remote site, with a concrete or steel foundation to absorb vibration.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the rotor and tether
buildSteps.detail: The tether is made from high-strength carbon fibre, balanced to spin at thousands of revolutions per minute without failing.

buildSteps.title: Install magnetic bearings and drive
buildSteps.detail: The rotor is suspended magnetically and coupled to a high-power electric motor that gradually spins it up.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the projectile
buildSteps.detail: The payload is packed into an aerodynamic shell, with electronics hardened to survive thousands of g.

buildSteps.title: Pump down and spin up
buildSteps.detail: Air is removed from the chamber, and the rotor is accelerated over minutes or hours to release speed.

buildSteps.title: Release and fly out
buildSteps.detail: At the correct angle the projectile is released through an exit port, flying a ballistic arc into the upper atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Kick to orbit
buildSteps.detail: A small rocket motor on the projectile provides the final velocity and circularises the orbit.

buildSteps.title: Recover and reuse
buildSteps.detail: If reusable, the projectile or its carrier is recovered, inspected, and prepared for another launch.

prerequisites.why: carbon fibre composites can carry the loads, but must withstand repeated high-speed cycles.
industrial vacuum pumps and seals can evacuate the chamber, though keeping it sealed during release is hard.
some rugged electronics and dense materials survive thousands of g, but most satellites do not.

prerequisites.tech: High-power electric drive and magnetic bearings
prerequisites.why: used in flywheels and centrifuges, but scaling to launch speeds is demanding.

prerequisites.tech: Small kick motor and thermal protection
prerequisites.why: upper stages and heat shields are mature, but must be adapted for the release conditions.

prerequisites.tech: Precise release timing and trajectory control
prerequisites.why: requires millisecond timing and aerodynamic modelling of a hypersonic projectile.

pathway.milestone: suborbital test flights from a vacuum centrifuge
pathway.unlocks: proof that the spin-up and release sequence works.

pathway.milestone: orbital launch of a small payload
pathway.unlocks: a propellant-free first stage for cubesats and rugged cargo.
lower cost per kilogram for bulk materials.
using the same principle where atmosphere is absent, e.g. from the Moon.
